_doc: VO is the timing backbone — scene length = measured VO duration + 0.6s pad, NOT target_sec. ReceiptGuard heist arc: cold open (a confident hallucination) → the ask → how it can't lie → LIVE run (baseline hallucinates, guard verifies + ships) → LIVE catch (inject a fabrication, guard catches it) → LIVE ledger reveal (signed receipts + hash chain VERIFIED) → reframe StatPunch → logo. SplitScreen graphic is NOT implemented in this build; the baseline-vs-ReceiptGuard contrast is captured LIVE (the demo UI is itself a split view) and the outcome is a data-driven StatPunch. capture:null = motion graphic; capture:'captures/x' = LIVE app footage over http://localhost:8000 (never a recreation).

scenes.vo: A support agent just told a customer their refund was approved. Two hundred and forty dollars, credited. It sounds finished. It sounds confident.
Except that refund never happened. The agent made the tool result up. ReceiptGuard makes that structurally impossible.

graphic_props.line: Tool result hallucinated — no refund record exists.

scenes.vo: So we give it one job. Resolve this refund ticket, end to end — and prove every tool result it acts on.

graphic_props.label: The one job
graphic_props.task: Resolve this refund ticket — and prove every tool result

scenes.vo: Every tool call runs through a gateway that signs its result with a receipt. Every claim the agent writes is cross-checked against those receipts. No receipt, no ship.

graphic_props.line: Every tool result is signed. Every claim is cross-checked.

scenes.vo: Watch it live. It plans with Qwen3-Max, signs every tool result, types every claim to a receipt, and ships only what's backed. The baseline agent, on the left, hallucinates. ReceiptGuard, on the right, does not.

Now inject a fabrication it never earned — a fifty-dollar goodwill credit with no receipt behind it. The baseline ships it. ReceiptGuard catches the unbacked claim, explains exactly why, and regenerates a clean, fully-grounded reply.
Every decision lands on an append-only, tamper-evident ledger. Signed receipts, hash-chained. Change one row and the whole chain breaks.
On our self-authored adversarial set: a hundred percent of fabrications caught, zero false positives. We tested exactly what we claim.
ReceiptGuard. A support autopilot that acts only on what it can prove, and escalates the rest to humans. Built on Qwen3-Max, Qwen-Flash, and Alibaba Function Compute.

graphic_props.tagline: Acts only on what it can prove.
